newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-GANZ KEEPS INTER ON COURSE IN UEFA CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GANZ KEEPS INTER ON COURSE IN UEFA CUP.

text.p: Second-half substitute Maurizio Ganz struck 15 minutes from time to pull Internazionale out of trouble and earn a hard-fought 1-1 draw with Anderlecht in their UEFA Cup quarter-final first leg on Tuesday.
Ganz's strike, after goalkeeper Geert De Vlieger fumbled a surprise overhead kick by Marco Branca, cancelled out a 27th minute goal by Bruno Versavel.
Versavel blasted an unstoppable half-volley from just outside the box past Gianluca Pagliuca from a Tibor Selymes pass from the left.
Inter -- bidding to win the UEFA Cup for the third time in seven seasons -- made the early running but left plenty of space for Anderlecht's speedy wingers in the first half.
But the Italian favourites raised the tempo after the break and Ganz came closest to the winner when he hit the post in the 88th.
"It was a very, very difficult match. Their goalkeeper had a good game but was unlucky in the end. However, we kept working and came away with a satisfying result," Inter coach Roy Hodgson said.
But Anderlecht coach Johan Boskamp sounded a clear warning to the Italians. "It isn't over yet," he said. "We looked a bit tired at the end but that is something we will work on."

Anderlecht, UEFA Cup winners in 1983, were brimming with confidence after Versavel's thunderbolt strike and ran Inter ragged on the wings to set up chances for Nigerian Celestine Babayaro and Versavel.
Versavel nearly caught Pagliuca off-guard just before the interval when he hammered a low shot from the right which the goalkeeper failed to hold. But Yaw Preko was too late to pounce on the rebound.
In the first half Inter's Ivan Zamorano twice cut through the home defence but failed to find the net.

He nodded just high in the 32nd minute after Youri Djorkaeff curled a free kick on to the Chilean's head, and was denied just in time by Anderlecht defender Samuel Johnson inside the box three minutes later.
Zamorano was on target again early in the second half when Djorkaeff tipped the ball cleverly backwards but De Vlieger punched clear.
De Vlieger again denied Inter the winner when he stopped a vicious Djorkaeff free-kick in the 68th.
"Anderlecht's marking was very aggressive, the ball moved around very well," Hodgson said. "They scored a fantastic goal."
